school_name: University of North Carolina School of the Arts
title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named UNCSA campus spaces with documented student uses, from meeting and study areas to creative-community venues.

cards.title: Hanes Student Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus center for meals, meetings, and activities
cards.notes: Use the Commons as a practical meeting point: it is documented for eating, socializing, meetings, and organizing activities.
cards.short_summary: A central student-services and gathering building.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says Hanes Student Commons provides space for students, faculty, and staff to eat, socialize, meet, and organize activities.
cards.access_notes: Campus facility; consult Student Affairs for meeting-space reservations.

cards.title: Eisenberg Social Hall
cards.subtitle: Ground floor of Hanes Student Commons
cards.notes: Plan student gatherings or attend campus programming here; the hall has ballroom and multipurpose-room configurations.
cards.short_summary: A flexible social hall inside the student commons.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA describes Eisenberg Social Hall as a large ballroom and smaller multipurpose room that can be used separately or combined.
cards.access_notes: Groups reserve Commons spaces through the Campus Portal Calendar or Student Affairs.

cards.title: The Well and TV Lounge
cards.subtitle: Inside Hanes Student Commons
cards.notes: Choose this named lounge when coordinating a low-key break or a casual conversation between classes and rehearsals.
cards.short_summary: A designated lounge within the campus hub.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA lists The Well and TV lounge among the facilities in Hanes Student Commons.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hanes Student Commons; access is subject to campus building operations.

cards.title: Hanes Student Commons Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Computer lab in Hanes Student Commons
cards.notes: Use the named computer lab for a focused work session when a shared campus workstation is more useful than a lounge seat.
cards.short_summary: A workstation option in the student commons.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA lists a Computer Lab among the facilities in Hanes Student Commons.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hanes Student Commons; use follows current campus technology and building policies.

cards.title: Library and Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus library and study destination
cards.notes: Meet for a quiet study block or join the documented Wednesday Mindful Lunch Hour held in the Library.
cards.short_summary: The campus library also hosts a weekly mindfulness gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA identifies the Library and Learning Commons on its campus map and says its Mindful Lunch Hour meets in the Library every Wednesday.
cards.access_notes: The campus map identifies this as Library and Learning Commons; verify current library access before visiting.

cards.title: Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Next to Artist Village
cards.notes: Schedule a movement break, group exercise, or student-organized game-club activity using the gym, aerobic room, and weight area.
cards.short_summary: Student-accessible fitness space with classes and game-club use.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says students are automatically Fitness Center members; the center offers group exercise and student-organized sport and game clubs.
cards.access_notes: UNCSA lists semester hours: Monday–Thursday 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; Friday 7 a.m.–6 p.m.; weekends 11 a.m.–5 or 10 p.m. Check seasonal changes.

cards.title: Artist Village
cards.subtitle: College residence hall at the north end of campus
cards.notes: For resident students, use the lounges, gaming areas, floor studies, or community kitchens to connect outside class work.
cards.short_summary: A residence hall built with several shared student spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says Artist Village includes gaming areas, community lounges, kitchens, studies on each floor, and laundry facilities.
cards.access_notes: College residence hall; exterior doors use computerized keyless entry and are restricted to UNCSA affiliates.

cards.title: Connector Building
cards.subtitle: High School Life community and study building
cards.notes: High school students can use its study rooms, computer lab, arts studio, kitchen, and multipurpose social-gathering space.
cards.short_summary: A High School Life building combining study, creative, and gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says the Connector Building houses High School Life offices, study rooms, a computer lab, arts studio, kitchen, and a large multipurpose space for student social gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Intended for High School Life; ask Connector Building staff about current room reservation and access arrangements.

cards.title: Daniels Plaza
cards.subtitle: Named outdoor campus plaza
cards.notes: Watch for campus welcome programming and use the plaza as a clear landmark when meeting fellow students outdoors.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor gathering site used in new-student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA's undergraduate orientation schedule places New Student Welcome Sessions at Daniels Plaza.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus location; event setup and availability vary by the university calendar.

cards.title: Crawford Hall
cards.subtitle: Gray Building performance venue
cards.notes: Check campus calendars for student-facing performances, meetings, and workshops; orientation programming has included Open Mic Night here.
cards.short_summary: A music-complex venue used for student programs and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA's orientation schedule lists an Open Mic Night in Gray Building's Crawford Hall, and UNCSA identifies it as a campus venue.
cards.access_notes: Performance and event access depends on the program; consult the UNCSA calendar or venue staff.
